Maya (AcmeCorp): Hey team — during yesterday's nightly backfill we saw a ~10min burst of 429s even though the console showed ~120 burst credits for our org. We're doing streaming completions at ~200 rps for ~2k concurrent requests for a short window. Example response headers we captured below. Any ideas?

Maya (AcmeCorp): ```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Thu, 03 Mar 2026 07:12:33 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: req_3fa2b1
X-RW-Burst-Credits: 0
X-RW-Burst-Allowed: 120
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded"}```

Sam (Support): Thanks — sorry about that. Can you paste the org id and the approximate UTC window (start/end)? Also did you see any fallback/region errors in the logs? If you have a few representative request_ids (like req_3fa2b1) that helps.

Maya (AcmeCorp): Org: org_67890. Window: 2026-03-03T07:05:00Z -> 2026-03-03T07:15:00Z. Attached a short snippet from our client logs: `req_3fa2b1`, `req_3fa2b7`, `req_3fa2c0`. Dashboard snapshot at 07:07 shows burst credits = 118.

Maya (AcmeCorp): Client log snippet: ```[07:06:57Z] req_3fa2b1 START stream tokens_est=120
[07:06:57Z] req_3fa2b1 429 X-RW-Burst-Credits=0
[07:06:58Z] req_3fa2b7 START stream tokens_est=200
[07:06:58Z] req_3fa2b7 429 X-RW-Burst-Credits=0
[07:09:20Z] req_3fa2c0 START stream tokens_est=30
[07:09:20Z] req_3fa2c0 200 OK X-RW-Burst-Credits=117```

Sam (Support): Okay — couple of common things to rule out quickly: 1) client-side concurrency ramps: if many requests start at the same millisecond they can all draw from the burst bucket before it refills. 2) streaming semantics: streaming requests can hold in-flight reservations and cause effective short-term drain. 3) fractional refill + smoothing can make the dashboard number look higher than immediately available credits at a given instant.

Sam (Support): Can you try a short run with concurrency capped at 50 and keep the same traffic shape? Also include the raw `X-Request-Id` headers from any 429 responses next time — we can map those to infra traces.

Raj (SRE): Quick background from infra: burst credits are consumed at admission time based on the request's estimated immediate token demand. Refill is continuous but applied in small fractional increments every few seconds (not instantly). If you have a tight fan-out (200 rps all starting at t=0) the system may admit N requests that each consume credits and push the bucket to 0 before the next fractional refill tick. The dashboard aggregates and samples, so the UI number can be slightly stale relative to per-request admission decisions.

Raj (SRE): Also note streaming requests sometimes reserve credits for the expected first chunk; if the client opens streams concurrently you get transient pressure. We saw a small capacity event in us-west-2 at 07:06 which created a short fallback to cross-region nodes for a subset of requests (we're pulling logs now). That can change admission heuristics for a few seconds.

Lina (Platform): Short mitigations: - enable client-side rate-smoothing (spread starts over 30s), - add jitter/backoff on 429 (exponential with small base, e.g., 200ms + jitter), - consider bumping baseline throughput (reserve) for your job window or request a temporary reserve from us. Longer term we can tweak smoothing policy for heavy backfills.

Lina (Platform): Example quick client change: ```js
// naive token-pacer to cap concurrent starts
const maxConcurrent = 50;
// hold queue and pop with 50ms spacing + jitter
```

Sam (Support): For diagnostics we've pulled traces for the three request ids; they show admission attempts from multiple frontend pods at the same ms and X-RW-Burst-Consumed values summing to your dashboard-full amount. We're continuing to collate exact pod ids and the 07:06 capacity blip.

Raj (SRE): TL;DR: not a billing bug — likely short, parallel drain + tiny regional capacity fallback + dashboard sampling. We can do two things: 1) remove any per-request reservation for very short streams for your org during the backfill (temporary policy tweak), or 2) grant a short reserved capacity bump for the 10-minute window. Which would you prefer for an immediate fix?

Maya (AcmeCorp): Thanks — a temporary reserved bump for the 10-minute window sounds easiest. We'll also implement client-side smoothing/jitter. If you can apply the tweak today that'd be great.

Sam (Support): Noted — I'll open a short-term reserve request and loop in billing ops. @Raj @Lina can you apply the policy tweak for org_67890 for 07:05-07:20 UTC and confirm?

Raj (SRE): I'll apply a temporary lenient smoothing policy for that org and time range, and flag the pod ids that hit the fallback so Platform can follow up. Will post confirmation in ~10m. (reacted :white_check_mark:)

deploy-bot: deployment org-policy-updates/lenient-smoothing applied to org_67890 by Raj at 2026-03-03T07:09:40Z

Maya (AcmeCorp): Confirmed — no 429s during a short retest at 07:12. Thanks everyone. We'll keep you posted if it reappears.

Sam (Support): Great — leaving this thread open one more day to monitor, but closing unless you see it again. cheers :thumbsup:
